To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of fuzzy output error as the performance function in training neural networks provides a significantly better classification of tutorial eye movements to reading scores than the use of mean square error as the performance measure.

the use of a fuzzy output error (as the performance function for neural networks training) can provide significantly better classification results when the data sets are imbalanced, and the use of a feed-forward neural network with three layers of neurons can give better classification results than a feed-forward neural net with two layers of neurons when the data sets contain imbalanced data.
the use of the fuzzy output error as a performance function in neural network training provides better performance for imbalanced eye gaze data sets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of eye gaze data for predicting reading comprehension scores and the effect of imbalanced data sets on the classification of eye movements.
the use of FOEs for training feed-forward neural networks to classify eye movements to reading and answering tutorial and quiz material.
the development of a neural network based model for predicting reading comprehension from eye gaze data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FOE as the training performance function is better for training neural networks for imbalanced data sets than MSE.
FOE outperforms MSE in training artificial neural networks to predict reading comprehension from eye gaze.
FOE outperforms MSE as a performance function for training artificial neural networks to classify eye movements to reading performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FOE is a better performance function to use for training neural networks when the data set is imbalanced.

the use of fuzzy output error (as the performance function for neural network training) can be used as an effective tool to overcome the negative effect of imbalanced data sets on classifier performance.
FOE is a more robust performance function than MSE when training neural networks to classify eye movements to reading performance and is recommended for use in other applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FOE is a useful alternative performance function for training artificial neural networks when the data is imbalanced.
the choice of performance function can have a significant effect on the performance of neural networks in classifying imbalanced data sets.
the choice of performance function is critical to the performance of the neural network.
